subject: Re: CloudBridge pilot — dedicated capacity sizing & weekly sync
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah@cloudbridge.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for CloudBridge pilot - sizing and ETA

Hi Connor / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudBridge is ready to move forward with a 6-week pilot (customer data, internal models). We want to understand what dedicated GPU capacity we should reserve for predictable latency and to avoid noisy-neighbor issues. High-level asks: 

- Support a peak of ~40 concurrent inference workers (chat + reranking) with typical seq len ~1024.
- Burst tolerance for 1.5x peak during demo days (2–3 days in the pilot).
- Data isolation and SOC-2 evidence will be required (we'll coordinate security separately).

Can you share a recommended slot configuration (GPU type, slot counts, expected p95 latency) and a proposed go-live date window? Also wondering how this maps to finance — rough monthly burn is fine for now.

Attached: CB_proposal_v1.pdf (pilot scope).

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Product, CloudBridge AI

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah@cloudbridge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CloudBridge pilot - sizing and ETA

Hi Sarah — great to hear you're ready. Quick notes and next steps below.

Short answers up front: we can size a dedicated pool that meets your peak targets and provide a weekly ops sync for the pilot. We typically propose a small reserved baseline plus burst slots to hit 1.5x.

To make a precise recommendation we need:
- Expected tokens/sec or requests/sec estimates at peak (if you have telemetry)
- Model family + preferred precision (32/16/8-bit) and whether you want quantized builds
- SLA target (p95 latency target; 200–600ms depending on model)

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Marcus to share current fleet slot availability and a tentative slot allocation.
2) Laura to confirm sales forecast / expected start date so finance can pro-forma burn.
3) Weekly 30m ops cadence starting next Monday (9am PT) to review usage and scale.

I'll loop infra and finance here. Marcus / Ben, can you run a quick slot-scenario for 40 concurrent workers + 1.5x burst and post a short table by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah@cloudbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CloudBridge pilot - sizing and ETA

Connor / Laura — ran a quick sizing pass and attached the snapshot. High-level that maps to Sarah's asks: 

Baseline scenario (recommended):
- GPU: 8x A800-like tiles (48GB) in dedicated pool 
- Slots: 12 concurrent model inference slots per GPU (depends on model quantization) => ~96 baseline concurrent slots
- Burst: +1.5x via pre-warmed burst pool (elastic) — add 48 slots for demo days
- Expected p95 latency: ~220–380ms for typical chat model at seq=1024 (depends on model and batching)

Notes / caveats:
- If they run a larger autoregressive model (no quantization), slot density drops ~30%, we should then recommend 12 GPUs baseline.
- We can enable KV-prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce token cost and lower latency during demos.
- SOC2 evidence: we have audit logs and KMS integrations — security team can provide the standard artifacts; I'll coordinate with Sarah's security contacts.

Attachment: fleet_capacity_snapshot_20290611.csv (contains slot math and tail-latency sims).

I recommend starting with the baseline above and enabling a Monday weekly check-in. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

Looping in finance questions so we have a clean ask for legal/procurement: 

From a billing perspective we'll need:
- Expected monthly committed hours for reserved GPUs (baseline) + estimated burst consumption (on-demand)
- Model family / token burn proxy (to price inference units if we do token-based billing)
- Whether CloudBridge wants a monthly reserved commitment or a short-term pilot pricing (we usually offer a pilot discount for 6 weeks)

I've attached q3_pipeline_burn.xlsx — Laura, can you drop the expected start date + ARR velocity into the yellow cells? I'll produce a quick pro-forma by Friday.

Ben Carter

Thanks everyone — confirming the cadence and action owners. Quick recap and MAP (mutual action plan):

MAP for CloudBridge pilot
- Owner: Laura Bennett (Sales) — finalize start date (target: 2029-06-24) and sign-off on scope.
- Owner: Marcus Lin (Infra) — provision 8 GPUs baseline + 48 burst slots; prepare access + monitoring dashboards (due: 2029-06-21).
- Owner: Ben Carter (Finance) — pro-forma cost estimate and pilot discount proposal (due: 2029-06-21).
- Owner: Connor O'Brien (Solutions) — run initial smoke tests, provide recommended p95 latency SLO and runbook.
- Owner: Sarah Lee (Customer) — provide model selection and rough requests/sec telemetry (due: 2029-06-18).

We'll start a 30-minute weekly ops call (Mondays 9am PT) starting 2029-06-24 to review actuals and adjust GPU counts. I've created a shared folder and added a draft runbook (weekly_runbook_draft.md) and the HubSpot deal link above.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
